numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For Yeo-Johnson log-likelihood, the implementation had numerical instability causing precision loss and overflow; it also handled empty inputs by returning a value (not specified here) and the fix explicitly added an `n == 0` early return of `_get_nan`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Compute the log-variance term in log-domain to avoid overflow and remove the constant term to avoid precision loss; for `n == 0` return `_get_nan(data, xp=xp)`.
trigger_conditions: Precision/overflow occurs for certain λ values where `abs(lmb)` or `abs(lmb - 2)` is very small (numerical instability when `abs(lmb)` or `abs(lmb - 2)` is very small).
All-positive or all-negative data (`xp.all(pos)` where `pos = data >= 0`) uses a special case to avoid overflow and precision loss.
Empty array along the reduced axis (`n == 0`).

oracle_clues: Bug title/description: `stats.yeojohnson_llf: fix precision loss and overflow` and PR text: `Remove constant term to avoid precision loss` and `Compute the log-variance term in log-domain to avoid overflow`.

The previous computation used `sigma = xp.var(y, axis=axis)` then `log_sigma` computed via `xp.log` with special handling: `finite_variance = sigma >= xp.finfo(sigma.dtype).smallest_normal` and `fill_value=-xp.inf`.
New behavior: cast to floating dtype via `dtype = xp_result_type(lmb, data, force_floating=True, xp=xp); data = xp.asarray(data, dtype=dtype`.
New behavior for empty input along the axis: `if n == 0: return _get_nan(data, xp=xp)`.
Clue about instability: `There exists numerical instability when abs(lmb) or abs(lmb - 2) is very small`.
Special case to avoid overflow/precision loss: `pos = data >= 0  # binary mask; if xp.all(pos): ...` (path for all-positive).

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: all-positive or all-negative data with example values [10, 10, 10, 9.9], and lmb regimes where abs(lmb) or abs(lmb-2) is very small; specifically lmb=-14, 16, -20, 20
category_specific_evidence: [discussion] When data is all neg/pos, remove the constant term can avoid precision loss; constant cannot be removed for mixed data.
[diff] Added dtype handling: dtype = xp_result_type(lmb, data, force_floating=True, xp=xp); data = xp.asarray(data, dtype=dtype).
[diff] Instability condition: “There exists numerical instability when abs(lmb) or abs(lmb - 2) is very small”.
[test_diff] test_gh24172 sets data = xp.asarray([10, 10, 10, 9.9], dtype=xp.float64) and evaluates yeojohnson_llf at lmb=-14, 16 (precision loss checks) and lmb=-20, 20 (overflow checks).
[test_diff] Precision loss expected values: yeojohnson_llf(-14, data) == 12.418595783381280 and yeojohnson_llf(16, -data) == 12.418595783381280 with rtol=1e-7.
[test_diff] Overflow expected values: yeojohnson_llf(-20, data) == 12.360966379200528 and yeojohnson_llf(20, -data) == 12.380287243698629 with rtol=1e-7.
reproduction_risks: Evidence only covers float64 and a specific example dataset; discrepancy conditions for other dtypes/precisions are not specified.
Evidence does not state an explicit numeric tolerance separating correct vs incorrect beyond using rtol=1e-7 for assert_close; other tolerances/decision thresholds are not provided.
Evidence describes instability when abs(lmb) or abs(lmb-2) is very small, but does not provide a concrete tolerance band or exact lmb values other than the tested ones (-14, 16, -20, 20).
